newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan envoy returns from secret mideast mission.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy returns from secret mideast mission.

text.p: Taiwan's top envoy returned from his latest overseas mission to the United Arab Emirates and Jordan on Saturday, vowing to continue the island's drive to break rival China's tightening diplomatic embargo.
Foreign Minister John Chang said he met senior government officials and members of the royal family in Amman and "very important friends" in Abu Dhabi. He declined to name them.
Taiwan media said he met Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan.
"The two nations greeted me with high courtesy...it was like treating a foreign minister from their diplomatic allies," Chang told reporters at Taipei international airport.
The minister said Jordan expressed a "strong desire" to boost relations. "This kind of contact is very significant and important," he added.
The United Arab Emirates and Jordan recognise Taipei's rival, Beijing, but both hosted Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui in 1995 despite fierce opposition from China.

Communist China, Taiwan's arch rival since a civil war split them in 1949, regards the island as a rebel province ineligible for foreign diplomatic ties and demands that other countries end links with Taiwan if they want diplomatic relations with China.
It has recently tightened its diplomatic squeeze on Taipei in its quest to bring Taiwan under mainland rule.
To evade China's diplomatic embargo, Taiwan officials have employed "secret diplomacy" -- unannounced visits to countries which recognise Beijing instead of Taipei.
Chang, who dropped out of sight on Tuesday, said Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government would continue to expand its international contacts.

"Our situation is rather unusual and difficult...but if we are brave and determined to develop and expand our contacts, it is impossible for mainland China to isolate the Republic of China from the international arena completely," Chang said.
He did not rule out more secret visits. "If there is a chance, I will go," he said.

China said on Thursday it strongly opposed Chang's visit to Jordan. It accused Taiwan's leaders of trying to disrupt its ties with other states and of lacking sincerity towards improving relations with Beijing.

"Mainland China's protest only irritates our host nations and shows how unreasonable they are," Chang said. But he added he had been forced to cancel meetings with "some friends" in Bangkok en route to Taipei becuase of media exposure.
Chang and Vice-President Lien Chan have between them visited Ukraine, Singapore, Malaysia, and Belgium over the last year in similar trips veiled in secrecy.
Earlier this month, Chang visited South Africa and sought in vain to reverse its November 27 decision to switch diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei by the end of 1997.
South Africa had been Taiwan's largest diplomatic ally. Some 29 other states still recognise Taiwan rather than Beijing.
